payload.prompt: Crie uma dimensão contabilística personalizada "Region" com os valores "Vestlandet" e "Midt-Norge". Em seguida, lance um documento na conta 6860 por 47500 NOK, vinculado ao valor de dimensão "Midt-Norge".

payload.goal: Create a custom accounting dimension 'Region' with values 'Vestlandet' and 'Midt-Norge', then post a voucher entry on account 6860 for 47500 NOK linked to dimension value 'Midt-Norge'.
success_checks: Custom dimension 'Region' is created and active in the chart of dimensions
Voucher is posted on account 6860 for exactly 47500 NOK
Voucher line is linked to dimension value 'Midt-Norge'
Voucher status is APPROVED/POSTED in the ledger
risk_notes: Custom dimensions may require a specific module to be enabled (e.g., 'Dimensions' module) — verify module activation before creation
Account 6860 must exist in the chart of accounts; if not, it must be created first
No voucher date specified — will default to today; confirm if a specific posting date is required
No counterpart account or balancing entry specified — a debit-only entry may fail validation; a credit account (e.g., 2900 or bank) must be provided
VAT treatment for account 6860 (typically an expense account) is unspecified — risk_notes: confirm if VAT applies
No voucher description/reference provided — may be required by system validation
Currency assumed to be NOK; confirm if multi-currency setup is needed
payload.suggested_first_action: Enable the 'Dimensions' module via POST /module if not already active, then create the custom dimension 'Region' via POST /customdimension.

line_items.description: Voucher entry on account 6860 linked to dimension 'Midt-Norge'

ordered_steps: 1. Check and enable 'Dimensions' module: POST /module {name: 'dimensions'} if not active
5. Verify account 6860 exists: GET /ledger/account?number=6860; create if missing
6. Identify or create a balancing account (e.g., credit account) for the voucher entry
7. Post voucher: POST /ledger/voucher with date=today, description='Region dimension posting'
8. Add debit voucher line: account=6860, amount=47500 NOK, dimensionValue='Midt-Norge' (customDimensionValueId: <Midt-Norge id>)
9. Add balancing credit line on appropriate account
10. Approve/post voucher: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:approve or confirm status is POSTED
11. Verify ledger entry: GET /ledger/voucher/{id} and confirm dimension linkage to 'Midt-Norge'

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Add new voucher. IMPORTANT: Also creates postings. Only the gross amounts will be used. Amounts should be rounded to 2 decimals.
Create a new free (aka 'user defined') accounting dimension
Create a new value for one of the free (aka 'user defined') accounting dimensions

rules: ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
When using vatType != 0 (e.g. VAT 25%), include ONLY the debit posting. Tripletex auto-generates VAT and credit postings.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
For salary/payroll vouchers, set employee={"id": employee_id} on each posting.
Always resolve account numbers via GET /ledger/account?number=XXXX first, then use account={"id": resolved_id}.
Postings with vatType={"id":0} (exempt) can include both debit and credit lines manually.

payload.text:
Let me analyze the task:

1. Create a custom accounting dimension "Region" with values "Vestlandet" and "Midt-Norge"
2. Post a voucher on account 6860 for 47500 NOK linked to dimension value "Midt-Norge"

Following the trace template:
1. GET /ledger/account?number=6860 - resolve expense account
2. GET /ledger/account?number=1920 - resolve counter-account (bank)
3. POST /ledger/accountingDimensionName - create "Region" dimension
4. POST /ledger/accountingDimensionValue - create "Vestlandet"


5. POST /ledger/accountingDimensionValue - create "Midt-Norge"
6. POST /ledger/voucher - create voucher with postings

I can run steps 1-3 in parallel since they're independent, but I'll need the dimensionIndex returned from step 3 before I can create the dimension values in steps 4-5. Looking at the schemas, AccountingDimensionName needs dimensionName, description, and active flag, while AccountingDimensionValue requires displayName, dimensionIndex, active, number, showInVoucherRegistration, and position.

Now I'm setting up the parallel requests for the first three steps.

I'll analyze the task carefully:

1. Create custom dimension "Region" with values "Vestlandet" and "Midt-Norge"
2. Post a voucher on account 6860 for 47500 NOK linked to "Midt-Norge"

Let me start with independent calls in parallel: resolve both accounts and create the dimension name.

payload.headline: Run aborted early due to LLM rate limit (429), only 1/6 checks passed.
what_went_wrong: LLM rate limit (429 RateLimitReached) hit after only 3 API calls, halting execution before dimension values or voucher were created.
Only account lookup (Check 1) succeeded; dimension 'Region', values 'Vestlandet'/'Midt-Norge', and voucher posting all failed.
The agent made two separate GET /ledger/account calls in parallel before the rate limit hit, consuming tokens without completing the task.
Scoring ended at 2.0/13.0 (0.3077) with 5/6 checks failed due to incomplete execution.
what_worked: Account resolution (Check 1) passed, indicating the GET /ledger/account call was correct.
POST /ledger/accountingDimensionName was correctly structured with 'Region' and active:true before the abort.
what_to_try_next: Retry the run during off-peak hours or reduce prompt/context size to avoid hitting the 50000 token/min uncached input limit.
Batch fewer parallel calls at once to reduce token consumption per minute; serialize dimension creation before voucher posting.
Consider caching account lookups or skipping redundant GET /ledger/account calls if account numbers are known, to reduce token usage.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/account (second call) — two parallel account lookups may be redundant if one call can fetch both accounts.
